# NPM Improved v1.7.7

## NPMX access-list and resource synchronization

- Include `/data/access` Nginx authorization files in the encrypted NPMX configuration snapshot. Previously the access-list database tables were included but their compiled htpasswd files were omitted.
- Repair missing or stale access-list authorization files on the primary from the stored access-list credential records before publishing a snapshot.
- Validate the access-list parent, client, authentication, and compiled authorization-file inventory before applying a snapshot.
- After Nginx generation and reload, verify synchronized database row counts, IDs, and access-list security fields, as well as file bytes and symlink targets for all synchronized filesystem roots. A mismatch fails synchronization instead of reporting false success.
- Preserve `/data/access` in the existing filesystem rollback snapshot so failed applies restore the previous access-control files and configuration.
- Preserve locally generated access-list files when restoring a legacy non-cluster backup that predates this new filesystem root.
- Run focused regression tests and syntax checks as a mandatory step in the release workflow.

## Resources covered by the NPMX snapshot

NPMX already includes users, permissions, authentication state, settings (except node-local NPMX pairing/settings), access lists, access-list usernames/passwords, access-list client CIDRs, certificates, proxy/redirection/dead hosts, streams, and configuration revisions. The filesystem snapshot includes custom Nginx, custom SSL assets, Let's Encrypt, and now the Nginx access files. Default-site templates are synchronized via settings and rendered locally using each node's variables. Node-local cluster pairing secrets are not synchronized.

## Deployment and validation

Upgrade primary and secondary to v1.7.7 through the existing Settings > Update workflow. Do not reset pairing or delete certificate/ACL state. Allow the secondary to complete a full pull or run Sync Now from the secondary.

Confirm that each access list, its users and CIDRs, and host assignments appear on the secondary. Test both permitted and denied HTTP requests through each node. Check NPMX Last Sync and Last Error. A successful status now requires post-apply inventory checks, but real traffic still requires explicit end-to-end verification.

The release workflow validates source syntax and audit regression tests before publishing GHCR and release bundles. No destructive migration is required.
